Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.chartCoord.text: This is the paper's radial σ. Lean often uses σ for period-one time in neighbouring declarations.

Breakdown.CertCell.labelFlip.text: labelFlip changes paper labels to (−ι₁, ι₂−ι₁); flipLabel changes generic frequencies to (n, −k). These are conjugate through labelHarmonic.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Is.text: The target_eq field makes the generic extended certificate's target gap zero on this cell route.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.IsPotentialSeri.text: The flux conditions join the radial and polar normal components in their respective directions, which supplies the weak divergence used in integration by parts.

Breakdown.CertReduction.AdjointSizeBound.text: The alternative to the cubic norm is the spatial L2 norm; it uses the supBoundFactor coefficient from the perturbation estimate.

Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.rows.text: The implementation stores row fields and nonnegative row weights separately. Absorbing the square root of each weight into its field gives the paper’s row seminorm.

Breakdown.CertCell.labelHarmonic.text: The multiplier library indexes modes by time and azimuth frequencies. The paper uses labels whose image is (2ι₂−ι₁, κι₁).

Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.pieceMultiplierDe.text: Positive and negative integrals are compared separately in ℝ≥0∞. Finite negative density permits the real subtraction used in (B.20).

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.treeState_ho.text: The local cell state may differ from its global embedding by gauge and constant-pressure shifts. The conditions on the forms make their values insensitive to those directions.

Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.patchGradSq.text: The rectangle Dirichlet energy includes the angular contribution k²|φ|²/r². This term survives although the test functions are stored on the (r,z) rectangle.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.hessTailGain.text: Off-axis coefficient tails and the physical radial-weighted energy use different measures. The source gain includes innerRadius and a 1/r₂ angular term in that normalization.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.pointwiseQua.text: A negative lower enclosure for the curl-gradient coefficient is allowed because its actual coefficient is nonnegative. The proof handles that branch separately, and also allows a zero diagonal in the final two-by-two test.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.IsDirectionR.text: The paper describes a radius depending on direction. The formal input additionally records measurability and fixed positive lower and finite upper bounds.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.complexCo.text: The real and imaginary parts occupy separate indexed columns. They can be zero or dependent; separate indexing records the maximum dimension lost to the negative-square terms.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.stateTerm.text: The source drops ignored pressure coordinates and allows the slaved coordinates to move linearly with the free variables. Its quotient-space argument is the general form of the paper's physical/free-coordinate decomposition.

Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.shiftValid_of_.text: The two indices represent the centre discrepancy and the parameter discrepancy. Their gradient-exponent flags select L² and L³, respectively.

Breakdown.CertReduction.adjointQuadCoeff.text: The L² adjoint branch uses the uniform bound on the perturbation. The norm supplied for the adjoint is L² in that branch, and L³ in the other branch.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.AzimuthalBounded.text: The injective label is the triple (complex component, time frequency, azimuthal order). Repeated triples must be combined before the squared-amplitude budget is formed.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.RemainderDualBou.text: This endpoint stores iterated integrability. Joint absolute integrability in the paper is obtained using finite weighted amplitude norms and the separate weighted-pairing lemma.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.PotentialData.text: The fields theta and phi represent G_j and U_j. The flux is encoded as a linear map from a differentiation direction to the output vector, so its displayed matrix is transposed relative to the paper's derivative convention.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.PotentialNorms.text: The numerical matrix budgets use the Frobenius square matSq, whereas the analytic decay interface uses the operator norm. An existential decay constant may absorb norm equivalence, but a numerical certificate budget must retain the specified norm.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.AdjointDefectEnt.text: The skew derivative of each pin generator introduces only a gradient difference from its Laplacian in the general interface. That difference vanishes when paired with a divergence-free perturbation.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Ad.text: The general adjoint bridge permits fitted directions with their own potentials. This cell specialization requires the fitted set to be empty, leaving the centre potential and the free-shift terms of B.12.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Of.text: An off-diagonal coefficient already adds both ordered terms. Only the upper triangle is summed, and the diagonal occurs once.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Is.text: The source frame entry is indexed by actuator first and adjoint second: frame(l,j) corresponds to the coefficient of beta_l in the paper's row V_j. The pairing uses a closed ball, which differs from the printed open ball only on a null sphere.

Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.isExtendedCert.text: The existential witness changes only the decay bound. The certificate record retains the given profile, periods, multiplier, pins, adjoints and numerical budgets.

Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.pieceMultiplierDe.text: The closure proves the multiplier construction and its extended-real density comparison for generic symmetry sets, weights and an explicit weak Hessian. B.1 specializes that data and converts the comparison to a real inequality after assuming finite negative density; the manuscript gives that conversion. The source does not supply a concrete admissible weight family.

Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.extendedCoerciveC.text: The source starts with the assembled RowMultiplierInequality and arbitrary admissible constants, rather than with B.20 and B.21 separately. Combining the two density inequalities gives that premise, and its scalar conclusion specializes to B.2.

Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.modeDensityBri.text: The formal bridge gives separate nonnegative integral identities for the mode densities and stretching term, with explicit lattice and symmetry inputs. Subtraction when the negative integral is finite produces B.23; it also covers infinite positive integrals without an undefined subtraction.

Breakdown.CertCell.cellLayerParts_closed.text: This declaration packages the proved analytic cell components as conditional implication statements. It is the implementation route for B.4, rather than a literal theorem with B.4’s four corrections and its quantifiers; applying the components to the finite entry conditions gives the reconstruction here. It supplies no numerical entries.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.angularModeP.text: After reading the source frequency pair as (time frequency, azimuth), the statement gives the four almost-everywhere angular and curl inequalities displayed in B.35. The source keeps the weak derivatives as separate fields.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.pointwiseQua.text: The source theorem is a scalar implication for abstract nonnegative derivative sizes, coefficient domination and the four angular inequalities. Substitution of the actual mode sizes gives B.5’s nonnegativity assertion; the intermediate lower bound B.36 is displayed here in the proof.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.modeRayInver.text: The rewrite makes the formal radius hypotheses explicit: measurability, positive-ray homogeneity, and uniform positive lower and finite upper bounds. With these conditions and the source weak perturbation fields, the displayed modal inverse-square estimate is the source conclusion.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.exteriorCond.text: This closure proves soundness of the packaged exterior conditions, joining ray and square inverse-square bounds with coefficient domination and the angular scalar test. The rewritten B.6 is the ray specialization and its integrated scalar argument; the square case comes from B.4.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.signedTre.text: The source retains the root-front quadratic form in its lower bound and needs only the abstract node inequalities and unique-parent bookkeeping. B.41 follows by discarding that form under the paper’s nonnegative-root condition; the real and complex enclosure theorems establish the node inequalities used here.

Breakdown.CertCell.rowRestClause_closed.text: This is the explicit cell-hypothesis-to-row-estimate formulation used by the source. The printed B.8 uses a partly unwritten condition list and a signed global form; the source passes through a meridional state and then recovers the same required estimate. Literal equivalence of the two complete finite condition lists is unavailable because the paper does not state one in full.

Breakdown.CertReduction.gapTransferBridg.text: After the cell assembly selects its two discrepancy pieces, this is the norm estimate (7.19) in B.9 with the same L²-gradient and L³-gradient costs. The frozen-form conclusion is supplied separately.

Breakdown.CertReduction.frozenFormBridge.text: For the reference field, this gives B.9's lower bound with the strain cost and the L³-gradient cost. The profile-change estimate then supplies the additional error.

Breakdown.CertReduction.formShiftBridge_.text: For the two chosen discrepancy pieces, this gives the change-of-form contribution of B.9, including the factors 1/(2 sqrt(w_*)). It combines with the reference estimate to give the printed c₃ bound.

Breakdown.CertReduction.adjointQuadratic.text: With the fixed cell adjoint, the conclusion is B.10's quadratic pairing bound with the same two sufficient norm choices. The abstract bridge also permits parameter-dependent adjoints.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.dualBoundedBound.text: The norm inequality is the one in B.11, and the source permits tests without a periodicity hypothesis over the chosen interval. Its endpoint records iterated integrability; the printed joint-integrability assertion is recovered by the separately explained weighted-norm argument and source integrability lemma.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.adjointDefectBri.text: In the paper's cell specialization, this bridge gives exactly the B.12 budget, but its standalone analytic interface explicitly requires potential weak derivatives, sharper Laplacian decay and the curl-potential density data. Relative to the coarse printed potential assumptions alone, these are extra hypotheses. The source's finite shape constructors supply them for a full CellSystemCondition.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.of.text: For the prescribed cell profile and zero target gap, this gives B.13's offset estimate. The source uses a closed ball with a null boundary and the same upper-triangular quadratic coefficients.

Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.isExtendedCert.text: This is the source's explicit construction of an extended certificate from fifteen finite-data fields and closed analytic bridges. It preserves the given record except for a derived decay bound, while the paper states a certificate directly under conditions that it partly omits. The conditional certificate conclusion is aligned, but literal equality of the full hypothesis formats is not claimed.

Breakdown.CertCell.formNegFinite.text: The theorem proves finiteness of the quarter-plane formNeg for every weak perturbation, from azimuth order at least one, uniform coefficient lower bounds and weak reference-profile regularity, with an arbitrary form-coercivity constant. It requires no right-hand-side equation involving F or β. Setting the constant to 3/50 and applying the separate negative-part density bridge identifies 4π·formNeg with I⁻, giving the negative-part finiteness assertion used in B.4 and B.8.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.representationHo.text: This is the weak adjoint-pairing identity underlying the integrations by parts in B.12. Its interface explicitly includes the decaying curl potential and the solenoidal test-density hypotheses; the subsequent potential, parameter and pin bounds supply the lemma's final numerical conclusion.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.of.text: This gives the same almost-everywhere quadratic residual expansion used in the proof of B.13 after the profile pieces agree inside the matching ball. The diagonal occurs once and each off-diagonal coefficient combines its two ordered terms; the coefficient enclosures and tail estimate are supplied separately.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.remainderAzimuth.text: This proves the finite harmonic component of B.11's dual estimate with the same improved denominator and component weights. It packages spatial and scalar-time integrability, while the printed lemma also includes the plain remainder and joint absolute integrability, obtained through the separately identified steps.

Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.spaceBreakdown.text: This is the conditional space-breakdown consequence obtained by supplying the closed analytic bridges and composing the cell-to-certificate construction with the later certificate and profile implications. B.14 itself concludes that the supplied objects form a certificate; this declaration proceeds to the stated consequence on space and retains the full CellSystemCondition hypothesis.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.weightedPairingI.text: This auxiliary theorem establishes joint pairing integrability from weak-gradient energy and a finite weighted L² norm of the other field. It supports the integrability assertion in B.11 after the finite mode representation is shown to have that weighted norm, but does not itself state the azimuthally improved dual estimate.

Breakdown.CertReduction.adjointQuadTerm_.text: This supplies the almost-everywhere time-slice absolute estimate used in the proof of B.10, with the same L² or L³ adjoint norm choices. The numbered lemma concludes an integrated period pairing bound, which the separate adjointQuadraticBridge_of declaration obtains from this slice result.
